      Validation rules

        KPI definitions and reporting logic
        KPIDefinitionSQLTableau calculated field
        Denial RateShare of submitted claims the payer denied.AVG(CASE WHEN claim_status = 'Denied' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)SUM(IF [Claim Status] = "Denied" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT([Claim Id])
        Reimbursement RatePaid amount as a share of billed charges.SUM(paid_amount) / SUM(billed_amount)SUM([Paid Amount]) / SUM([Billed Amount])
        Denied RevenueBilled charges on denied claims.SUM(CASE WHEN claim_status = 'Denied' THEN billed_amount ELSE 0 END)SUM(IF [Claim Status] = "Denied" THEN [Billed Amount] END)
        Pending A/RBilled charges on claims not yet adjudicated.SUM(CASE WHEN claim_status = 'Pending' THEN billed_amount ELSE 0 END)SUM(IF [Claim Status] = "Pending" THEN [Billed Amount] END)
        Avg Processing DaysMean days from claim submission to adjudication.AVG(processing_days)AVG([Processing Days])
        • Payer level. The dataset records each claim's plan type (PPO, HMO, EPO, POS) and region, not the insurer's name, so payer performance is compared by plan type.
        • Reconciliation. Billed charges should equal paid + denied + pending + any shortfall on approved claims. The tie-out is checked on every filter.
        • Synthetic data. In this dataset, claim statuses were assigned at roughly 85% approved, 9% denied and 6% pending, and approved claims were paid in full, so differences between groups are small.
        • Data: 162,178 synthetic claims from the public insurance-claims-dashboard project (nourhan-ali-ml), engineered from a Kaggle medical insurance dataset.
        • Audit sample: 12,845 synthetic adjudicated claims with allowed amounts, member cost-sharing, denial reasons and flagged billing patterns, joined to member payer type, from the public Healthcare_claim_cost_analysis1 project (shubhamdataanalytic5). A reimbursement record is inconsistent when paid + deductible + copay + coinsurance + coordination of benefits differs from the allowed amount by more than $1 on a claim that was not denied.

        KPI definitions and reporting logic
        KPIDefinitionSQLDAX measure
        Total VisitsER visits in the selected period.COUNT(*)Total Visits = COUNTROWS('ER')
        Admission RateShare of visits admitted as inpatients.AVG(CASE WHEN admission_flag THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)Admission Rate = DIVIDE( CALCULATE([Total Visits], 'ER'[Patient Admission Flag] = TRUE()), [Total Visits])
        Average Wait TimeMean minutes from arrival to being seen.AVG(wait_time)Avg Wait = AVERAGE('ER'[Patient Waittime])
        Over Wait TargetShare of visits waiting longer than the target (SLA, default 30 minutes).AVG(CASE WHEN wait_time > 30 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)% Over SLA = VAR sla = SELECTEDVALUE('SLA'[Minutes], 30) RETURN DIVIDE( COUNTROWS(FILTER('ER', 'ER'[Patient Waittime] > sla)), [Total Visits])
        SatisfactionMean score (0–10) over visits that gave one; most visits didn't.AVG(satisfaction_score)Avg Satisfaction = AVERAGE('ER'[Patient Satisfaction Score])
        • Dates. Admission dates in the source are day-first (dd-mm-yyyy hh:mm). Parsing them with a US locale swaps day and month for dates up to the 12th and shifts weekday counts, so they're parsed with an en-GB locale (in Power Query: Using locale → English (United Kingdom)).
        • Department is the department the patient was referred to. Visits with no referral are kept as "No referral".
        • Data: public Hospital ER dataset (Hospital ER_Data.csv), 9,216 synthetic emergency room visits.

            Method, cleaning and feature engineering
            • Data: UCI "Diabetes 130-US Hospitals for Years 1999–2008" (Strack et al., 2014), — de-identified inpatient encounters.
            • Cleaning: removed — encounters discharged to hospice or that ended in death (they cannot be readmitted) and 3 with unknown gender; treated "?" as missing; grouped ICD-9 codes for primary and secondary diagnoses into 9 clinical groups; kept the 10 most common admitting specialties.
            • Target: readmitted within 30 days (readmitted = '<30').
            • Engineered features: age as an ordinal, total prior visits (outpatient + emergency + inpatient), number of diabetes medications prescribed and changed, any diabetes diagnosis, plus encounter counts, length of stay, lab procedures, A1C and glucose results, discharge disposition, admission type and source, and payer.
            • Validation: 80/20 split by patient, so no patient appears in both training and test data; 5-fold cross-validation grouped by patient on the training set; class weights balance the 11% positive rate. Models: scikit-learn LogisticRegression, RandomForestClassifier (300 trees) and HistGradientBoostingClassifier.
            • Recall is the share of readmitted patients the model flags as high risk; precision is the share of flagged patients who were readmitted. Lowering the threshold raises recall and lowers precision.
            • SQL: SELECT number_inpatient, AVG(CASE WHEN readmitted = '<30' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) AS readmit_rate FROM encounters GROUP BY number_inpatient;

              Diagnostic Errors

              Confusion matrix on held-out tumors. Missed malignant cases are the costly error.

                Method and evaluation
                • Data: Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer dataset (UCI; bundled with scikit-learn): 30 measurements of cell nuclei from fine-needle aspirate images (mean, standard error and worst value of radius, texture, perimeter, area, smoothness, compactness, concavity, concave points, symmetry and fractal dimension).
                • Split: 80/20 stratified train/test split (seed 42). The test set was scored once, after tuning.
                • Pipeline: StandardScaler → SelectKBest (ANOVA F-test) → model. The number of features and each model's main hyperparameter were tuned with 5-fold cross-validation on the training set (ROC-AUC). Feature selection kept all 30 measurements for Logistic Regression, Random Forest and SVM, and 20 for KNN.
                • Threshold for recall: each model's threshold was set where it catches 97% of malignant tumors in out-of-fold training predictions, then applied unchanged to the test set.
                • Metrics: malignant is the positive class. Precision = flagged tumors that were malignant; recall = malignant tumors flagged; F1 = their harmonic mean.
                Interactive web version. Charts, KPIs and model scores are computed in the page from the embedded data and held-out model predictions; cross-validation scores and feature importances come from the Python training run.
